html:
Kuala Lumpur began in 1857 as a tin-mining camp where the Klang and Gombak rivers meet, after a Selangor prince sent Chinese miners up the river to open mines at Ampang. Its name means muddy confluence.

It grew under the Chinese leader Yap Ah Loy, who rebuilt it after the Selangor civil war of the 1860s and 1870s. The British made it the capital of Selangor in 1880 and of the Federated Malay States in 1896, after the Pangkor Treaty.

It became the capital of Malaya at independence in 1957 and of Malaysia in 1963. The Petronas Towers rose there in 1998. See also the tin rush and Chinese migration.
